newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S. Africa assessing Mandela's Middle East visit.
newsitem.headline: S. Africa assessing Mandela's Middle East visit.

text.p: South African Deputy Foreign Minister Aziz Pahad met Arab diplomats on Friday to discuss the Middle East crisis and its possible effect on President Nelson Mandela's planned visit to the region in November.
"The visit has already been postponed once. It would be a rather serious scenario that would lead us to decide not to go ahead in November," foreign affairs spokesman Pieter Swanepoel told Reuters.

He said Pahad told representatives of the Palestinian Authority, Jordan, Egypt, Morocco and Lebanon that the government would monitor the situation "with the president's visit in the backs of our minds".
Pahad met Israel's ambassador on Thursday to discuss clashes in which more than 50 people died in two days.
Presidential spokesman Parks Mankahlana said the situation would remain under constant review, but there was no immediate change to Mandela's programme.
"We are keeping a close watch...it is something that has to be looked at from all angles. But as things stand at the moment, the president is still going," he said.

Mandela is scheduled to visit Israel, the Palestinian self-rule Authority, Jordan and Egypt from November 4 to 12 on a mission originally planned to bolster five years of successful peace moves in the region.
"The purpose of the president's visit was to lend encouragement to the peace process in the Middle East," said Swanepoel.
He said the visit would be assessed on the basis of its appropriateness under the circumstances at the time and in terms of Mandela's security.
"I think it will be a bit of both. Obviously, we don't want to send the president into a situation that could be unsafe."
